findings.claim: Examiners reward located detail.
findings.truth: No examiner statement is quoted or citable. The advice itself is sound, so it is restated without attributing it to examiners.
findings.evidence: house rule: no fabricated examiner claims

findings.claim: Tarn Hows in the Lake District attracts more than 750,000 visitors a year. Repeated in the exam tip, practice question 5 and a flashcard.
findings.truth: No published source gives 750,000. Wikipedia records 'over half a million visitors per year in the 1970s', and half a million is the figure used in GCSE resources. Reduced to 'more than half a million', which is true under every published figure found.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Tarn Hows

findings.claim: Eduqas examiners often ask you to explain how a single landform forms.
findings.truth: House rule: an Eduqas/WJEC lesson never names the board in student-facing prose. Reworded to 'the exam'.
findings.evidence: house rule

findings.claim: this is a recurring error highlighted by markers
findings.truth: No marker report is quoted or citable. The warning is kept without the invented attribution.
findings.evidence: house rule: no fabricated examiner claims

findings.claim: High Force on the River Tees has retreated to leave a gorge over a kilometre long.
findings.truth: The gorge below High Force is about 700 metres long.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, High Force: 'The length of the gorge is currently about 700 metres (2,300 ft).'

findings.claim: Eduqas markers reward answers that link the three factors rather than listing them.
findings.truth: Names the board in student prose (house rule) and invents a marker claim. Reworded so the advice stands on its own.
findings.evidence: house rule

findings.claim: the chalk cliff at Birling Gap in East Sussex lost up to seven years' worth of erosion in a single weekend
findings.truth: The 'about seven years' worth' loss at Birling Gap is reported for the 2013-14 winter storm season as a whole (roughly 3 m of cliff over that winter), not for one weekend. No source supports a single weekend, and the surrounding sentence already frames the winter. Changed to 'a single stormy winter', a strictly weaker and safe statement.
findings.evidence: could not reach a primary source (BBC blocked, National Trust page 404); the claim is reduced rather than replaced with a new number

findings.claim: Eduqas examiner reports flag two recurring errors with hydrographs.
findings.truth: Names the board (house rule) and cites an examiner report that is not quoted or citable. Reworded.
findings.evidence: house rule

findings.claim: mark schemes reward you for weighing costs against benefits and reaching a clear judgement
findings.truth: No mark scheme is quoted; house rule also forbids pasting board mark-scheme wording. The instruction is given directly instead.
findings.evidence: house rule

findings.claim: Examiners flag the misconception that hard engineering is always better
findings.truth: No examiner statement is citable. The point is kept as direct advice.
findings.evidence: house rule: no fabricated examiner claims

findings.claim: The Environment Agency divides UK floodplains into Flood Zones 1 (lowest risk) to 3b (highest risk).
findings.truth: The Environment Agency's remit is England only. Natural Resources Wales publishes the flood map for planning in Wales and SEPA does so in Scotland. This matters on a board with many Welsh centres.
findings.evidence: Environment Agency remit (England); NRW / SEPA equivalents

findings.claim: Around 2,000 homes and 1,000 businesses were flooded across the Calderdale district, and damage exceeded 100 million pounds. Repeated in practice question 5 and a flashcard.
findings.truth: Calderdale Council's own Boxing Day 2015 reporting is commonly cited at a higher level (roughly 2,700 homes and 1,500 businesses). I could not reach a primary source in this session (council page 404, Wikipedia gives no Calderdale figures). Options: leave as an understated 'around' figure, or raise all three places to the council's published counts once confirmed. Recommendation: confirm against the Calderdale Flood Commission report, then raise; do not edit blind.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia 2015-16 Great Britain and Ireland floods gives no Calderdale property counts; calderdale.gov.uk page returned 404
findings.ruling: Leave: unverified figure or band-ladder queue item.

findings.claim: Three people died and around 1,800 homes flooded [Carlisle, January 2005]. The figure is repeated in the exam tip and a flashcard.
findings.truth: Published values disagree. Wikipedia's Carlisle article says '2,700 homes were flooded and three people died'. The Environment Agency figure used in most GCSE resources is about 1,900 properties. The death toll of three is correct in both. Recommendation: move to 'around 1,900 homes' (the Environment Agency count) in all three places, or leave and accept the low end; do not adopt 2,700 without a second source.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Carlisle: '2,700 homes were flooded and three people died'
findings.ruling: Leave: unverified figure or band-ladder queue item.

findings.claim: Every 3, 6 and 8 mark scheme in the unit uses a four-step ladder named Mastering / Secure / Developing / Emerging (18 mark schemes across six lessons).
findings.truth: These are invented band names, not the board's and not the house set (Top band / Upper-mid band / Mid band / Lower-mid band / Low band). They are not factually wrong, so this is a bulk relabel rather than a fact fix. Recommendation: fold into the programme's existing band-ladder queue rather than editing here.
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md house band vocabulary
findings.ruling: Leave: unverified figure or band-ladder queue item.

findings.claim: the chalk cliffs of the Seven Sisters lose only a few centimetres
findings.truth: Published research puts recent Seven Sisters / Beachy Head retreat at tens of centimetres a year, well above 'a few centimetres', although the long-term historic rate was that low. No settled figure was reachable this session, and the contrast with Holderness still holds either way.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia Beachy Head and Seven Sisters give no rates

findings.claim: Lowlands such as East Anglia and the Thames Basin sit on softer, younger rocks like chalk and clay (L1) versus 'Hard, well-cemented rocks like granite or chalk resist erosion' (L4).
findings.truth: Both usages are standard - chalk is a soft rock in the upland/lowland sense but resistant at the coast, where it forms headlands. Students do confuse the two. Not wrong, so no edit; worth a sentence of signposting if the unit is ever rewritten.
findings.evidence: internal cross-lesson comparison

findings.claim: Park-and-ride buses serve Honister and Buttermere on busy days
findings.truth: Honister and Buttermere are served by seasonal bus routes (the Honister Rambler). I could not confirm a park-and-ride scheme at either. Not mark-affecting - either would be credited as visitor management.
findings.evidence: no reachable source for a Honister/Buttermere park-and-ride

findings.claim: The lower River Severn, controlled by reservoirs in mid-Wales, deposits less than it did a century ago.
findings.truth: The general mechanism (dams trap sediment) is sound and Llyn Clywedog does regulate the Severn, but this specific comparative claim is unsourced.
findings.evidence: no reachable source

findings.claim: Around 5 % of homes built in England since 2009 have been on Zone 3 floodplains.
findings.truth: Published analyses of new homes in English flood zones use different base years and different zone groupings, and report figures from about 5 % up to about 10 %. Could not confirm this exact pairing of figure and start year.
findings.evidence: no reachable official statistic this session

findings.claim: reduces peak flood levels in Belford village by an estimated 30 %
findings.truth: Published Belford results are usually given as a reduction in peak FLOW of roughly 15-30 %, not peak level, so 30 % is the top of the range and the wrong quantity. The figure is also the key to knowledge check 4, so any change needs both.
findings.evidence: Belford runoff attenuation scheme reporting

findings.claim: Storm Eva dumped over 100 mm of rain on the upper Calder Valley in West Yorkshire in a single day ... The River Calder rose 2 metres in a few hours
findings.truth: Both are plausible for 26 December 2015 but neither could be confirmed against a gauge record this session.
findings.evidence: no reachable source

summary: Content and process teaching are accurate and match Core Theme 1 scope exactly; all 30 knowledge-check keys and all 6 matching sets are correct, and the 8 marks plus 4 SPaG practice label matches the spec (84 marks plus 4 SPaG for this paper). The real damage is in the exam tips: three name the board and six invent examiner or mark-scheme claims. Two case-study figures were corrected against published values (High Force gorge, Tarn Hows visitors) and one unsupported timeframe was reduced (Birling Gap).
